question: Which of the following phyla contains Leech?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Option 4: Annelida**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Leeches belong to the phylum **Annelida**, which is characterized by segmented bodies.
 
• Annelids, commonly known as segmented worms, include earthworms, leeches, and polychaetes.
 
• Leeches are mostly found in freshwater environments, though some species live in terrestrial and marine habitats.
 
• The class Hirudinea includes leeches, which are known for their use in medicine, particularly for their anticoagulant properties.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Phylum Annelida**:

 
 
• Annelida is a large phylum of segmented worms, which includes approximately 17,000 species.
 
• Annelids have bilateral symmetry and a true coelom (body cavity).
 
• They possess a hydrostatic skeleton that aids in movement and flexibility.
 
 
 
• **Leech Anatomy**:
 
 
• Leeches have a flattened body with 34 segments.
 
• They possess two suckers, one at each end of their body, used for attachment and movement.
 
• Many leeches have specialized structures for feeding, including jaws and pharyngeal glands.
 
 
 
• **Medical Use of Leeches**:
 
 
• Leeches have been used in medicine for centuries, primarily for bloodletting and to stimulate circulation.
 
• Their saliva contains anticoagulants, anesthetics, and vasodilators, making them useful in modern microsurgery and reconstructive surgery.
 
 
 
• **Reproduction in Annelids**:
 
 
• Most annelids reproduce sexually, and some species are hermaphroditic (possessing both male and female reproductive organs).
 
• Leeches typically lay eggs in cocoons, which are deposited in the environment.
